caption: ROUGE-1 metric for fine-tuning MBart and T5 models with adapters with different r with WikiHow dataset
model_annotation: The plot titled “Finetuning for different r, WikiHow” illustrates how the ROUGE-1 score changes as a function of the adapter rank setting (shown as log r) for four model–adapter combinations. The x-axis is labeled “log r” and uses a linear scale with integer tick marks from 0 to 9 at a regular interval of 1. The y-axis is labeled “ROUGE-1” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 0 up to just under 40, with major tick marks every 5 units (0, 5, 10, …, 35). Four solid lines with circular markers are shown: the red line (T5 + LoRA) starts near 23 at log r=0, rises to around 28–29 by log r=4–5, and then gradually decreases to around 27 by log r=9; the blue line (MBart + LoRA) begins near 12 at log r=0, dips to around 5 at log r=1, then increases to around 27 by log r=4–5 and remains near 27 through log r=9 with a slight decline at the end; the green line (T5 + AdaLoRA) starts near 23 at log r=0, increases steadily to around 36 by log r=4, and then stays nearly flat around 36 through log r=9; the orange line (MBart + AdaLoRA) starts near 12 at log r=0, rises to around 21 by log r=2 and around 29 by log r=3, then continues increasing more gradually to around 33–34 by log r=7–9, where it levels off.
